'''Maximilian Weigend''' (born September 25, 1969, in Erbendorf) is a German botanist.  

== Biography ==
As a student, Weigend received first prize in 1987 and 1989 as part of the Federal President's history competition on the subject of environmental history and in 1992 from the [[South African Phycological Society]] for his studies on the [[phytochemistry]] of South African [[macroalgae]].<ref name="main">{{cite journal|first1=Maximilian |last1=Weigend |title=Loasaceae |journal=[[Flora de Colombia]] |volume=22 |publisher=Instituto de Ciencias Naturales, Universidad Nacional de Colombia  |location=Bogotá |date=2001 |pages=99–100 |language=es |issn=0120-4351}}</ref>

In 1993, he graduated from the South African University of Natal-Pietermaritzburg and then moved to [[LMU Munich]]. As part of his research, he traveled to Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru before commencing in July 1997 with his dissertation ''Nasa and the conquest of South America – Systematic Rearrangements in Loasaceae Juss''. He received his doctorate degree magna cum laude. As part of this work, Weigend presented a complete revision of the flower nettle family (''[[Loasaceae]]'') and re-described numerous genera and species, but due to a technical error the taxa had to be revalidated in 2006.<ref>[[International Code of Botanical Nomenclature]] (Vienna Code), Art. 30.5, Ex. 10, [https://ibot.sav.sk/icbn/no%20frames/0034Ch4Sec1a030.htm Online]</ref> He received several awards for his dissertation.<ref name="main"/>

From 1999, Weigend began research on the genera ''[[Ribes]]'' and ''[[Desfontainia]]''; in 2000 he became an assistant professor at the Institute for Systematic Botany and Phytogeography at the [[Free University of Berlin]].<ref name="main" /> In 2011 he was appointed to the [[University of Bonn]], where he succeeded Wilhelm Barthlott as director of the [[Botanical Garden, Bonn
]].<ref name="bonn">{{cite web|url=http://www.botgart.uni-bonn.de/o_uns/weigend.php |title=Maximilian Weigends Homepage |publisher=Botanische Gärten der Universität Bonn |access-date=2022-08-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160301055402/http://www.botgart.uni-bonn.de/o_uns/weigend.php |archive-date=2016-03-01}}</ref> Since then, he has also been deputy director of the Nees Institute for Plant Biodiversity.<ref name="bonn2">{{cite web|url=https://www.nees.uni-bonn.de/staff/pages/weigend-prof.-dr.-maximilian |title= Personal page|publisher= Nees Institute for Plant Biodiversity}}</ref>

Weigend has edited the ''Loasaceae'' for several standard works, such as in 2001 for the ''[[Flora de Colombia]]'' and in 2004 for the sixth volume of the ''[[Families and Genera of Vascular Plants]]''.

Weigend is married, and is a father of two children.<ref name="bonn"/>
